LESSONS.t: Drugs that change in kidney failure

cls.w: Block adrenaline at the heart: slower, gentler beats. Timolol does it in the eye too.
Block calcium in artery walls so arteries relax and BP drops.
Block angiotensin; can cause dry cough and angioedema.
Block angiotensin's receptor; no cough, so it's the usual swap.
Stop platelets from clumping. Together = DAPT after a stent or coil.
Lower lipids and steady plaque.
Boost GABA, the brain's brake. Fast calm; dependence and respiratory depression.
Keep serotonin around longer. Weeks to work.
Serotonin plus norepinephrine, so BP can rise.
Older antidepressant; anticholinergic; deadly in overdose.
Stops monoamine breakdown; tyramine → hypertensive crisis.
Seizure drugs that also calm mania.
Block dopamine hard: positive symptoms, lots of EPS.
Block serotonin + dopamine: positive AND negative symptoms, metabolic side effects.
Relax smooth muscle (prostate, vessels): orthostatic hypotension.
Shrink the prostate slowly over months.
Stop acetylcholine breakdown. Brain (Alzheimer's) or eye (echothiophate). Can slow HR.
Blocks excess glutamate; moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's.
Drains fluid out of the eye.
Acts like acetylcholine: constricts the pupil, opens drainage.
Blocks prostaglandins: pain and inflammation down, bleeding risk up.
Severe pain; respiratory depression; reversed by naloxone.
Pulls fluid off; potassium drops.
Sends sugar out in the urine; protects the kidney.
Replaces erythropoietin to make RBCs.
Gives back dopamine activity (used for NMS).

use.w: Lower the force on the weak wall. Beta blockers first-line; ACE/ARB/CCB second-line; nicardipine IV pre-op.

use.l: Prevent clots after stent or coil

use.w: Benzos work fast; buspirone is scheduled and slow.
Phentolamine IV or nifedipine SL brings BP down fast.
Mood stabilizers. Lamictal is for maintenance.
Antipsychotics: 1st gen for positive symptoms, 2nd gen for positive and negative.
Diphenhydramine for dystonia; dantrolene + bromocriptine for NMS.
Drain fluid out, or (timolol) make less of it.
Fluoxetine = bulimia; Vyvanse = binge eating; thiamine before refeeding.
Alpha blockers relax it now; 5-ARIs shrink it over months.
Pain control; tamsulosin helps the stone pass.
Protect the kidney, fix anemia, remove fluid, keep dialysis tubing open.
Boost acetylcholine, block glutamate; sertraline for mood/impulsivity.

warn.w: Platelets or clotting are blocked: watch gums, stools, bruising.
Vessels relax or BP reflexes are blunted, so standing up drops BP.
Beta blockade or extra acetylcholine slows the heart.
Norepinephrine, more RBCs, a stimulant, or tyramine (MAOI).
Too much serotonin: agitation, tremor, fever, sweating.
CNS depressants; worse together or with alcohol.
Withdrawal seizures (benzos), rebound HR/BP (beta blockers), discontinuation symptoms (SNRI).
Less aldosterone, so the kidney keeps potassium.
ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs, and diuretics make the kidney hold lithium.
Failing kidneys clear less, so dose down or avoid.

warn.l: Small pupils: poor vision in dim light

tamsulosin: Works right away on urine flow
finasteride: Pregnant women shouldn't handle crushed tablets

bromocriptine: Gives back dopamine activity in NMS

lisdexamfetamine: First drug approved for binge eating disorder

lithium: Drink 2–3 L a day, steady salt
NSAIDs and diuretics raise the level

alprazolam: Respiratory depression with alcohol or opioids

phenelzine: Avoid aged cheese and smoked meat

lisinopril: Hold as ordered: dialysis drops BP

pilocarpine: Report flashes or a curtain over vision

nicardipine: IV drip with an arterial line

losartan: The usual swap when cough happens

morphine: Dose needs review in kidney failure

dapagliflozin: Sends sugar out in the urine
furosemide: Works only while kidneys still make urine
